extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house counsel, law firms, legal analysts, and business decision-makers using legal analytics
extracted.subtask_description: A year-in-review analytics report summarizing quantitative metrics and methodology for U.S. patent litigation (district courts, PTAB, ITC) to inform venue selection, budgeting, strategy, and competitive intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: New cases filed (annual and monthly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of new patent cases filed (e.g., 'In 2016, 4,537 patent cases were filed - a 22% decline from 2015'). Includes month-by-month and year-by-year charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use year and month breakout to identify filing trends and seasonal spikes; account for rule changes (e.g., elimination of Form 18) that can affect raw filing counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant-case pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Counting each defendant in a case separately (defendant-case pairs) to normalize for the AIA's anti-joinder rule, which limits suing multiple defendants in one case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use defendant-case pairs to compare pre- and post-AIA filing activity meaningfully, since raw case counts are affected by joinder rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-volume plaintiff definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina defines a high volume plaintiff as a plaintiff who has filed at least 10 cases within a 365 day span.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter analytics by (or exclude) high-volume plaintiffs to examine different litigation patterns; high-volume plaintiff litigation is more variable and drives district concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top districts / district concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics showing distribution of new cases by district (e.g., E.D. Tex. had 1,662 cases and ~36.7% of 2016 filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use district share and changes by quarter/year to inform venue selection, transfer strategy, and to assess jurisdictional exposure; watch concentration (e.g., E.D.Tex + D.Del ≈ all other districts combined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case timing (medians and variability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median times and distribution to key events such as claim construction hearing, trial, preliminary injunction, permanent injunction (e.g., median preliminary injunction 3.8 months, permanent 11.6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare median and boxplot dispersion across districts to budget time and money, and to set client expectations; use district-specific timing for scheduling and flat-fee planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary judgment metrics (filing and grant rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates at which summary judgment motions are filed and granted/denied/partially granted; E.D.Tex shows lower filing and grant rates relative to other districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret low filing/grant rates (and local requirements to seek permission) as factors increasing settlement likelihood due to increased trial risk and obscuring denied-motion statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to stay pending PTAB (grant rate and time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics on motions to stay pending PTAB decided in 2015-2016, including grant/deny/partial rates and median decision timing for top districts (e.g., E.D.Tex, D.Del, N.D.Cal had similar grant rates of 55-60%; C.D.Cal. denied more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use district-specific stay grant probabilities and timing to decide whether to pursue a stay pending PTAB and to budget for motion-related expense and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent litigation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and trends for cases asserting design patents vs utility patents (design litigation is more consistent and concentrated in C.D.Cal; C.D.Cal saw a 4.8% increase over 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track asserted-patent type and district concentration to forecast caseload and to tailor venue/strategy for design vs utility patent disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA litigation definition and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: ANDA cases identified as patent infringement cases prompted by an ANDA or paper NDA filing; excludes investigational drugs, OTC, biosimilars, generics authorized by branded maker. Metrics include year, month, and top districts (heavily concentrated in D.N.J. and D.Del).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing Hatch-Waxman litigation, include ANDA and paper NDA cases together and use specialized timing/remedy expectations (e.g., judge trials, stipulated infringement, date-bound injunction remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge caseload and findings metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of new cases and case outcomes by judge (e.g., Judge Gilstrap assigned 1,119 cases in 2016 and leads in findings and summary judgments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze individual judge caseloads, assignment practices, and decision patterns when making venue/transfer and litigation strategy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party-level metrics (top plaintiffs/defendants and plaintiff types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rankings and profiles of top plaintiffs and defendants (e.g., top plaintiffs in 2016 were Shipping and Transit, Uniloc, Sportbrain; top ten plaintiffs are patent monetization entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use party-level metrics for business development, outside counsel selection, and to anticipate opponent behavior (e.g., PMEs’ historical win rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law firm representation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and rankings of law firms by plaintiff-side and defendant-side representation nationally and within states (e.g., top defendant firm Fish & Richardson had 160 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark outside counsel on timing/results, and use firm-level data in law firm selection and competitive analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent findings by judgment type
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of how patent findings arise: 'Findings of infringement tend to come from either trial or from consent or default judgment, while findings of non-infringement or invalidity are more likely to have come from summary judgment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect different procedural paths for particular findings; use this to plan evidence, motion practice, and settlement strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity basis categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of patent invalidity findings by statutory basis (e.g., 101 Subject Matter, 102 Anticipation/Novelty, 103 Obviousness, 112 Definiteness/Enablement/Written Description) and metrics over time/district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track temporal and district trends in invalidity bases (e.g., §101 invalidations) to refine claim drafting, prosecution strategy, and defense planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case resolution taxonomy and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina generates a resolution for each case (e.g., terminated cases 2009-2016: 74.6% settled, 15.3% procedural outcomes, 6.1% claimant wins, 4.0% claim defendant wins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use resolution distributions to set realistic client expectations about settlement likelihood and to allocate resources toward litigation vs settlement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages frequency and distribution metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics on damages frequency (e.g., compensatory damages awarded in ~1.8% of terminated cases filed since 2000), totals, medians, percentiles, and skew (most awards small; a few outliers drive totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use percentile and median statistics (and log-scale visualizations) rather than means to forecast realistic damages exposure; expect jury awards to account for much larger cumulative totals than judge awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages by judgment type and by district
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of damages by judgment type (consent, default, judge, jury) and median compensatory awards by district (e.g., D.Del, E.D.Tex, E.D.Va among most generous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate district- and judgment-type-specific damages behavior into exposure calculations and settlement negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB petition and trial-flow metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IPR and CBM petitions by month and trial-flow diagrams from petition filing through final written decision, settlement, or procedural outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTAB trial-flow probabilities to assess the likelihood of institution, settlement, or final decision, and to weigh the strategic utility of PTAB petitions vs district litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC investigations and ALJ outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of ITC investigations filed over time and dispositive outcomes by current ALJ (e.g., cease & desist orders, general exclusion orders, settlements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ITC likelihoods and outcome patterns when assessing remedies and exclusion risks in product-oriented disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data methodology and case identification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina's data combines PACER, PTAB, ITC, Orange Book and other sources, adds algorithmic normalization and human review/hand-coding, actively analyzes complaints to identify patent cases and filters out spurious cases; data focused on lower courts (District Courts, PTAB, ITC) and excludes appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using analytics, understand underlying case-identification rules, human-coding practices, and scope limits (e.g., exclusion of appeals) to interpret metrics correctly and to replicate or compare datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxplot timing interpretation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of boxplots to convey timing: median (50th percentile), box bounds (25th to 75th percentiles), box compression/elongation indicates predictability, whiskers show reasonable bounds, outliers defined by convention (>1.5× IQR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret boxplots by median and interquartile spread to understand typical timing, predictability, and worst/best-case bounds for case events; rely on boxplots for budgeting and contingency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local court procedural practices affecting metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Local procedures (e.g., some E.D.Tex judges historically requiring a five-page letter brief seeking permission before filing a summary judgment motion) affect filing rates and grant statistics and therefore settlement rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust interpretation of motion and resolution metrics for local procedural practices that reduce filing frequency or alter grant/deny visibility (motions not filed do not count as denied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of timing analytics for strategy and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina recommends using timing analytics to inform counsel and client decisions (e.g., budgeting for claim construction takes less time in Central/Northern Districts of California than in E.D.Tex or D.Del).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply district-specific timing and variability to set flat fees, schedule conflicts, and to advise clients about likely litigation timelines and cash-flow impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live analytics and data-quality caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Live analytics may differ slightly from published charts due to Lex Machina’s ongoing data quality efforts and data normalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat published snapshot numbers as illustrative; consult live platform for up-to-date figures and expect occasional adjustments from data-cleaning efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform feature capabilities (analytics product enhancements)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of 2016 product features that affect available analytics: Attorney Data Engine (extracts attorney/firm data), Orange Book case columns (drug/ingredient mapping), Courts & Judges Comparator App, Law Firm Comparator App, Magistrate Judge Data, MDL handling, new timing events, Parties Comparator App, Damages Explorer, Help Center, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage platform features (attorney extraction, comparators, party/law-firm/damages explorers) to generate tailored analyses; be aware feature availability affects what queries/filters are possible.
